title: Diwali to Chhath 2026: Back to Back Travel Planning
summary: Two festivals, eight days apart. Compare staying through, two round trips, and split plans, with the leave maths for November 2026.
body_markdown:
Eight days separate Diwali on Sunday, 8 November 2026 from the main Chhath arghya on Sunday, 15 November. That gap is too long to sit idle in a hometown for most working travellers and too short to justify two full round trips comfortably. Almost every difficult decision in November comes out of those eight days.


# A Sane Approach to Diwali Chhath Back to Back Travel Planning


The mistake in most Diwali Chhath back to back travel planning is treating it as one long festive block. It is two separate events with different destinations, different peak nights and different return pressures, and the plan should reflect that.


## Three Ways People Handle the Gap


Each of these works for someone. The right one depends on how much leave you have, how far you are travelling, and who is travelling with you.


### Plan A: Stay Through the Whole Window


Travel out before Diwali, remain at home through Chhath, and return once on 16 or 17 November. Two travel legs instead of four, one set of bookings, and no time lost to the road in between. The cost is roughly a full working week away, which only works if your leave allows it or your job travels with you.


### Plan B: Two Separate Round Trips


Go home for Diwali, return to the city for the working week, then travel again for Chhath. It protects your work commitments and suits people whose leave is limited. The trade off is four legs booked on four of the tightest dates in November, which needs all four seats secured in advance rather than sequentially.


### Plan C: Split the Family


Elders and children travel out before Diwali and stay through, while working members join later for Chhath and everyone returns together. This spreads the load sensibly, though it needs the most careful booking, since one set of tickets is outbound early, another is outbound late, and the return is a group booking on a peak date.


**Plan** **Travel legs** **Working days away** **Suits**


Stay through Two Roughly a full week Flexible leave, remote work, longer corridors


Two round trips Four Around two to three Limited leave, shorter corridors, solo travellers


Split family Three or four Varies by member Families with elders, children or school schedules


## The Leave Maths for November 2026


The calendar is unusually kind this year, and working through it before applying for leave is worth the ten minutes.


- Diwali on 8 November is a Sunday, with Govardhan Puja on 9 November and Bhai Dooj on 10 November both observed as holidays in several states.
- The Chhath Sandhya Arghya on 15 November is also a Sunday, and 16 November is a state holiday in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttarakhand.
- Between them sits the working week of 11 to 13 November, which is the only genuinely contested stretch.
- Dev Deepawali on 24 November coincides with Guru Nanak Jayanti, a gazetted holiday, so anyone extending into Kartik Purnima has another anchor date to build around.


Holiday status varies by state and by employer, so confirm against your own state notification and office calendar rather than a general list. On the plan A route, three days of applied leave often covers the entire stretch from Diwali weekend to Chhath.


## Why This Particular Gap Causes Trouble


Families that observe both festivals face a genuine choice rather than a scheduling detail. Stay through and you lose a working week. Return in between and you pay for four travel legs on the busiest dates of the month.


What follows compares the three ways people actually handle it, works through the leave maths, and lists the bookings to make together. Live route options sit on the[zingbus route and city pages](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets) for your corridor.


## If You Stay Through, Plan the Working Days Properly


Staying through only works if the middle week is usable. Check network coverage and power reliability at the place you are staying, not the town it belongs to, because they are frequently different things.


Carry a backup connection, keep a charged power bank, and be honest with your team about which hours you will actually be available. The week between two festivals in a family home is not a normal working week, and treating it as one is what makes the whole trip feel exhausting.


## Packing for Ten Days Instead of Three


A stay through plan changes the packing problem completely. You are carrying clothes for two festivals, gifts for both sides of a family, work equipment and whatever the weather does between early and late November, when nights turn noticeably cooler across north India.


Baggage on zingbus services is capped at 15 kg per passenger, which a ten day family trip crosses easily. Distributing weight across travellers rather than one large suitcase is simpler than negotiating at the bus door, and fragile gift items belong in hand baggage rather than the hold.


## Travelling With Elders and Children Across Two Festivals


If elders are travelling out early and staying through, book them a lower berth and a boarding point that does not require a long walk or a connecting cab. School holidays rarely cover both festivals in full, so check the school calendar before committing children to a plan A stay.


For anyone travelling separately from the main group, a departure that arrives in daylight is worth choosing over a marginally cheaper one that arrives at 4 AM in a town where they will need to find transport alone.


## The Bookings to Make in a Single Sitting


Whichever plan you pick, make every booking it needs at the same time rather than as each date approaches. On a plan B trip that means all four legs together, and on a plan C trip it means both outbound bookings and the group return.


The corridors carrying most of this traffic are the long eastern ones. The[Delhi to Lucknow route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-lucknow-bus-route) runs a dozen daily departures, while the[Delhi to Gorakhpur route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-gorakhpur-bus-route) runs three, and that difference decides how much slack you have. Check the cancellation terms on the[policies page](https://www.zingbus.com/policies) before paying, particularly if your leave approval is still pending.


**Note:** Prices are approximate and may vary based on season, demand, and availability.


## Where These Plans Usually Break


Three failure points account for most of the trouble. The first is an unbooked return, which turns a well planned trip into a scramble on 17 November. The second is a middle week that was assumed to be workable and was not, which usually ends with someone travelling back at short notice on the worst possible date.


The third is treating a connecting leg as automatic. If you are travelling beyond a hub city to a village or a smaller town, that second leg needs its own booking and its own buffer, because an overnight bus that loses ninety minutes to festive traffic will not make a tight morning connection.


## Choosing Your Plan and Locking It Down


Look at your leave balance and the distance you are travelling, then pick one of the three shapes rather than improvising. Long corridors favour staying through, since four legs on a nine hour route in ten days is punishing. Shorter corridors make two round trips reasonable.


Once the shape is decided, the rest of the Diwali Chhath back to back travel planning is mechanical: every leg booked in one sitting, returns first, boarding points chosen for reliability rather than convenience, and connecting legs given room to breathe.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How many days apart are Diwali and Chhath in 2026?


Diwali on 8 November and the main Chhath arghya on 15 November 2026 are seven days apart, with the four day observance ending 16 November.


### Is it better to stay through or make two trips?


Staying through suits long corridors and flexible leave, while two round trips suit shorter corridors and jobs where the middle week cannot move.


### How much leave does Diwali Chhath back to back travel planning need?


Diwali Chhath back to back travel planning often needs only about three days of applied leave, since both festival days fall on Sundays this year.


### Which dates should I avoid travelling on?


Avoid 7 November and 13 November for outbound travel and 10, 11, 16 and 17 November for returns if your dates allow any flexibility.


### When should all the bookings be made?


Make every leg in one sitting through the second half of October, since booking each date as it approaches leaves the return legs exposed.


### Do school holidays cover both festivals?


School holidays rarely cover both festivals in full, so check the school calendar before committing children to a stay through plan.


### What if my leave is not approved yet?


Read the cancellation terms attached to your fare before booking, then book anyway, because seats on peak nights disappear faster than approvals arrive.


### Is working remotely from a hometown realistic during this window?


Working remotely is realistic if you verify network coverage and power reliability at the exact place you are staying, not the town generally.


### How should luggage be handled for a longer stay?


Distribute weight across travellers rather than one large suitcase, since the limit is 15 kg per passenger and gift items add up quickly.


### What about elderly parents travelling separately?


Book them a lower berth, a boarding point without a long walk, and a departure that arrives in daylight rather than the early hours.


### Do I need to book connecting legs separately?


Connecting legs beyond a hub city need their own booking and a comfortable buffer, because festive delays regularly break tight morning connections.


### Does Dev Deepawali affect this plan?


Dev Deepawali on 24 November is a separate window, though it coincides with a gazetted holiday and suits anyone extending the trip further.


### What is the single most common mistake?


Leaving the return leg unbooked is the most common mistake, since return demand concentrates on far fewer dates than outbound travel does.
